submission.natural_language_explanation: Delimited-span head: a token is predicted active while it sits inside a span opened by a delimiter the head reads back to — a quotation mark (" ' “ ‘ « „, including the bracket-quote compound token that opens a code string), a markdown _ or * emphasis marker, or an opening ( or [ — attending to that opening delimiter with weight 0.3-0.95 (the innermost opener when spans nest) and writing at a nearly depth-independent strength set mostly by which delimiter it reads (about 1.9-2.4 for a double-quoted span, 2.2-3.4 for _ or [, up to 4.9 in the scan). Predicted inactive: prose with no open delimiter before the token (20 of 20 varied sentences peaked at 0.49 against the 1.23 line), apostrophes in contractions and possessives, commas, colons and dashes, the opener itself, the closing mark and most text after it (a token or two just after a close can sit near the line, and after ] up to 1.7), and a quotation mark at the very first position of the prompt.

rival_explanations: Narrower class: only quotation marks (and markdown emphasis) open a span, so parenthetical asides, square-bracket insertions and code brackets are inactive and their scan activity comes from token identity rather than delimiters.

Broader class: any set-off punctuation within a few tokens is the cue, commas, colons, dashes or a closing mark as much as an opener, so colon lists, comma appositives and text just after a close are as active as quoted spans.

Lookahead: the head prepares the closing delimiter, so it should be strongest on the last word before a close and weak or absent at the start of a long span, rather than uniformly strong while the span is open.
